---
title: Containers
---

Containers go a step further than virtual environments.
They bundle our code with its software
and operating-system user-space dependencies while sharing a host kernel,
so we can reproduce that environment
on computers with a compatible container runtime and platform.

This part builds up to [docker-uv-renv](https://github.com/chendaniely/docker-uv-renv),
an example project whose image has Python and R,
their packages locked with uv and renv,
and Quarto for reports:

- [Introduction to containerization](../lectures/0610-containers.qmd)
  and [Using and running containers](../lectures/0620-containers-running.qmd)
  run images that other people built.
- [Customizing and building containers](../lectures/0630-containers-building.qmd)
  writes a first `Dockerfile` and builds it.
- [Python packages with uv in an image](../lectures/0640-containers-uv.qmd)
  and [R packages with renv in an image](../lectures/0645-containers-renv.qmd)
  put each language's packages in an image,
  and [Python and R in one image](../lectures/0648-containers-uv-renv.qmd)
  combines them into docker-uv-renv.
- [Docker Compose](../lectures/0650-containers-docker-compose.qmd) runs it,
  and [Working in a container over ssh with Positron](../lectures/0660-containers-ssh-positron.qmd)
  works inside it.
- [Containers outside class](../lectures/0690-containers-home-lab.qmd)
  lists apps that people run at home in containers.
